title: DeepSeek picks CITIC Securities to lead a Shanghai STAR Market IPO
subtitle: The AI lab is pursuing a listing on China's tech-focused exchange alongside an $8B pre-IPO round that would value it around ¥500B ($74.5B).
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: DeepSeek has selected CITIC Securities as a lead underwriter for a planned IPO on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market, according to reporting from Bloomberg and the South China Morning Post on September 9–10, 2026. The Hangzhou-based lab is also raising a pre-IPO round of roughly $8 billion at a valuation near ¥500 billion (about $74.5 billion), with a filing targeted for later this year and a listing that could arrive in 2027. Three additional underwriters have been engaged; the identities of two of them have not been reported.

The choice of STAR over Hong Kong is the story. Moonshot AI listed in Hong Kong earlier this month at a $50B valuation, and Zhipu, MiniMax, and 01.AI have all been reported as Hong Kong-listing candidates. DeepSeek picking the Shanghai STAR Market instead is a policy signal — STAR is the exchange Beijing built to keep strategic-tech listings onshore in RMB rather than in USD-linked Hong Kong. For an AI lab whose training runs on Huawei Ascend hardware and whose models are on the US export-control watchlist, listing in RMB reduces exposure to the sanctions surface. It also means Chinese institutional capital, not global capital, will price the stock.

The pre-IPO round overlaps with DeepSeek's ongoing V4.1 Flash production rollout (covered September 10) and its 160,000-chip Huawei Ascend 950DT cluster in Inner Mongolia (covered September 7). Together, those three items describe a lab that is simultaneously scaling compute, hardening a domestic hardware stack, and raising public-market capital — the same posture Anthropic has taken with its US IPO push (mid-October target, $2T valuation) and OpenAI has taken through its Astra commercialization. The three frontier labs are on close-to-identical financial timelines even as the geopolitics between them diverge.

Takeaway for learners: watch the IPO prospectuses when they land. A prospectus discloses model training costs, inference margins, customer concentration, and R&D headcount in a way that no marketing page does. When DeepSeek, Anthropic, and OpenAI file, you will get the first real numbers for what a frontier AI business looks like — revenue per active user, cost per token, capex intensity. That data will settle a lot of arguments about the economics of the field, and it is the kind of document worth reading closely if you want to understand where the industry is going.
